claim: A signed disposable Ubuntu guest automatically resumed the same native Dagu run after an orderly kernel reboot, preserved its checkpoint and produced one local effect. A dedicated read-only serial observer and independent journal review confirmed completion before postboot SSH; owned cleanup passed.
limitations: One orderly disposable guest reboot with a synthetic workload; not a physical PC, power loss, production disaster recovery, provider recovery or broker acceptance.
The unchanged official Dagu retry tests are a selected upstream subset. The project planner, its original 12-test oracle and the guest experiment are local synthetic integration coverage.
Source, disk and process continuity cover this owned guest only; no distributed exactly-once or arbitrary external side-effect guarantee.

Public text projections replace owned home prefixes and synthetic UUIDs and normalize CRLF. Original artifact/stream hashes and explicit projection rules are retained; projected bytes are not labelled raw-byte-identical.
The full auth-free guest archive contains three hidden bookkeeping files omitted by loose-file artifact upload. Independent inspection used the intact archive.
Both prior failed attempts remain failures; retrospective successful workload records did not override their missing acceptance evidence.
No model was called and no provider or lifetime token-saving measurement was made.
independent_review: A separate read-only reviewer independently fetched both platform artifacts, matched API digests, execution/source identity, native outputs, serial hashes/order, both journal boots, checkpoint/effect invariants and owned cleanup. No actionable findings remained.
